body.statement: Fix \((j,k)\in\vec E\) and a branch with \(b_jb_k\ge0\). If \(d_j(\mu)d_k(\mu)>0\), then \(Q_{jk}(b,\mu)\le0\) holds if and only if either \(b_j=b_k=0\), or \(b_jb_k>0\) and \(b_j/b_k\) lies between the two positive reciprocal calibration ratios \(d_j(\mu)/d_k(\mu)\) and \(d_k(\mu)/d_j(\mu)\). If exactly one of \(d_j(\mu)\) and \(d_k(\mu)\) is zero, then \(Q_{jk}(b,\mu)=-b_jb_kd_m(\mu)^2\le0\), where \(m\) indexes the nonzero coordinate. If both are zero, then \(Q_{jk}(b,\mu)=0\).
body.justification: The exhaustive zero-case identity gives a total polynomial replacement for divided calibration ratios on every component branch.
body.gap: HuntingtonKlein2026, Assumption 4 on pp. 17--18, uses conditional divided supershort ratios; it does not state this project-maintained polynomial generalization or its exact zero-coordinate cases.
body.consumer: The inference routine can evaluate every null at zero or local-to-zero coefficient changes without arbitrary clipping.
